CMS finalized separate hospital-outpatient payment status for Tauvid in 2027

Tauvid remains separately paid under hospital OPPS after temporary pass-through expires, under a different payment classification.

Key label details: Flortaucipir F18/Tauvid (HCPCS A9601) moves from temporary pass-through status G to separate payment status K.

BiomarkersTau PETTauAmyloidReimbursement

Added November 23, 2026 · cms-1850-fc-2027-pet-opps

Evidence summaryDesign, results, and what changed

Thirty-second field brief

Tauvid remains separately paid under hospital OPPS after temporary pass-through expires, under a different payment classification. Verify the relevant facility billing, applicable coverage and reimbursement rather than inferring them from the new K status alone.

Study design

CY 2027 OPPS final rule Table 7 and expiration of existing temporary pass-through payment.

Key label details

  • Flortaucipir F18/Tauvid (HCPCS A9601) moves from temporary pass-through status G to separate payment status K.
  • Its per-day cost exceeds the finalized $635 diagnostic radiopharmaceutical packaging threshold. The figure is a packaging threshold, not a payment amount.
  • Florbetapir A9586, flutemetamol Q9982 and florbetaben Q9983 also appear with K in the final table.

What changed

Flortaucipir F18/Tauvid (HCPCS A9601) moves from temporary pass-through status G to separate payment status K.

Strength of evidence

Final Medicare hospital outpatient payment rule. Key constraints: hospital outpatient opps, not all sites or payers.

Clinical and field impactInterpretation, implementation, and access

Clinical significance

Verify the relevant facility billing, applicable coverage and reimbursement rather than inferring them from the new K status alone.

Field medical relevance

Interpret alongside these constraints: Payment status does not determine which indications a contractor covers.

Quanterix or platform relevance

Verify the relevant facility billing, applicable coverage and reimbursement rather than inferring them from the new K status alone.

Access or reimbursement relevance

Medicare payment classification effective January 1, 2027; not a coverage or appropriateness determination.

Likely questionsWhat you may hear and what the evidence supports
Does this create national coverage for a tau PET indication?
No. It is a payment classification and not a new clinical coverage determination.
Critique and limitationsBias, uncertainty, and missing evidence
  • Hospital outpatient OPPS, not all sites or payers
  • Payment status does not determine which indications a contractor covers

Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services CMS-1850-FC, Table 7, Federal Register page 70321. 2026-11-06.
